perspective:
Keith’s available information:

- He works with Elizabeth at a construction company; she is the receptionist, and they interact in a friendly but professional way when he visits the office for paperwork and project updates.
- Over the past few days, Keith noticed Elizabeth being unusually curt with him.
- Keith believed she might be upset with him because of a misunderstanding or an unknown mistake he made.
- Keith asked Elizabeth if he had done something to upset her.
- Elizabeth told him no, not at all; she said she was dealing with personal stuff and apologized if she seemed short.
- Keith felt sympathetic and wanted to support her.
- Keith offered to talk and suggested a coffee break.
- Elizabeth accepted the coffee break and thanked him.
- During the coffee break, Elizabeth shared more about her stresses, which Keith perceived as quite severe.
- Keith suggested Elizabeth consider talking to a professional and mentioned an external perspective could help.
- Elizabeth told him she had thought about it but was unsure and hesitant about seeking help.
- Keith noticed Elizabeth became slightly withdrawn after his suggestion.
- Keith believed he might have embarrassed her and felt regretful.
- Keith told Elizabeth he hoped he had not overstepped, and that he wanted her to know he was there to support her no matter what.
- Elizabeth told him he did not overstep, that she appreciated his concern, and that it was a lot to think about.
- Later, Keith observed Elizabeth seeming more open and appreciative of his concern.
- Keith believed she valued his support and felt more comfortable around him.
- Keith told her he was glad they could talk and that he was always there if she needed to chat or take a break together.
- Elizabeth thanked him, said it meant a lot to her, and said she felt better knowing she had his support.
- Keith intends to maintain this supportive relationship with Elizabeth.
